title: Past perfect and past simple
summary: Past perfect для действия «до» другого прошедшего момента, когда его нужно (а когда нет), причины, нереализованные планы, hardly/no sooner с инверсией, by the time, косвенная речь и разница между когда-порядок и когда-одновременность.
ru:
## Что делает past perfect
**Past perfect** (had + V3) помещает действие **раньше другого момента в прошлом**. Это «прошлое в прошлом»: мы сначала называем опорную точку (past simple), а затем отсылаем к тому, что произошло до неё.
> When I got to the office, the meeting had already finished. — Когда я пришёл в офис, совещание уже закончилось.
> She felt calmer because she had spoken to her lawyer. — Ей стало спокойнее: она поговорила с адвокатом.
Если убрать had, смысл изменится. **When I got there, the film started** — фильм начался **после** моего прихода; **...the film had started** — он уже шёл.

## Когда past perfect не нужен
Если порядок событий и так ясен из **before, after, as soon as, once, until, when** и из логики, носители часто используют обычный past simple:
> After she finished / had finished her degree, she moved abroad. — Закончив учёбу, она уехала за границу.
> I locked the door before I left. — Я запер дверь, прежде чем уйти.
Но если важна **причина или результат** («почему так вышло»), past perfect уместнее:
> The streets were empty. Everyone had gone home. — Улицы были пусты. Все ушли по домам.
Правило: не ставьте had везде подряд; длинный рассказ в past perfect утомляет. Достаточно один-два раза показать «прошлое в прошлом», а затем вернуться в past simple.

## Причины и предыстория
Past perfect часто объясняет состояние в прошлом (чувства, внешний вид, итог):
> He was out of breath; he had run all the way. — Он запыхался: пробежал всю дорогу.
> I didn't recognise Pavel — he had lost a lot of weight. — Я не узнал Павла: он сильно похудел.

## Нереализованные планы и ожидания
С глаголами **hope, expect, mean, intend, want, plan, think** past perfect показывает, что **задуманное не осуществилось**:
> I had hoped to see you at the conference. — Я надеялся увидеть тебя на конференции (но не увидел).
> We had intended to leave early, but the traffic was awful. — Мы хотели выехать пораньше, но пробки были ужасные.

## Hardly, scarcely, no sooner
Для эффекта «едва… как» используют past perfect с инверсией (в письменной и торжественной речи):
> Hardly had the speaker sat down when the audience stood up. — Едва оратор сел, как зал встал.
> No sooner had we left than it started to pour. — Едва мы вышли, как хлынул дождь.
После **hardly/scarcely** идёт **when**, после **no sooner** — **than**.

## By the time и косвенная речь
> By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient had died. — К моменту приезда скорой пациент уже скончался.
> She said she had lost her passport. — Она сказала, что потеряла паспорт. (в косвенной речи present perfect и past simple сдвигаются в past perfect)
Также: **It was the first time I had flown alone.** — Я летел один впервые.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~When I arrived, the train already left.~~ → ...the train **had** already **left**.
- ~~No sooner I had sat down than...~~ → No sooner **had I sat** down than...
- ~~She told me she has lived in Rome.~~ → She told me she **had lived** in Rome.
en:
## What past perfect does
**Past perfect** (had + past participle) puts an action **before another moment in the past**. It is the 'past in the past': we first name the reference point (past simple) and then look back at what happened earlier.
> When I got to the office, the meeting had already finished.
> She felt calmer because she had spoken to her lawyer.
Take away had and the meaning changes. **When I got there, the film started** - the film began after I arrived; **...the film had started** - it was already running.

## When past perfect is not needed
If the order of events is clear from **before, after, as soon as, once, until, when** and from logic, native speakers often use plain past simple:
> After she finished / had finished her degree, she moved abroad.
> I locked the door before I left.
But if the **reason or result** matters ('why things were as they were'), past perfect fits better:
> The streets were empty. Everyone had gone home.
Do not put had everywhere; a long story in past perfect is tiring. One or two uses to show the 'past in the past' are enough, then return to past simple.

## Reasons and background
Past perfect often explains a state in the past (feelings, appearance, outcome):
> He was out of breath; he had run all the way.
> I didn't recognise Pavel - he had lost a lot of weight.

## Unfulfilled plans and expectations
With **hope, expect, mean, intend, want, plan, think**, past perfect shows that **the plan did not happen**:
> I had hoped to see you at the conference. (but I didn't)
> We had intended to leave early, but the traffic was awful.

## Hardly, scarcely, no sooner
For a 'just as' effect we use past perfect with inversion (written and formal speech):
> Hardly had the speaker sat down when the audience stood up.
> No sooner had we left than it started to pour.
After **hardly/scarcely** comes **when**; after **no sooner** comes **than**.

## By the time and reported speech
> By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient had died.
> She said she had lost her passport. (in reported speech present perfect and past simple shift to past perfect)
Also: **It was the first time I had flown alone.**

## Common mistakes
- ~~When I arrived, the train already left.~~ → ...the train **had** already **left**.
- ~~No sooner I had sat down than...~~ → No sooner **had I sat** down than...
- ~~She told me she has lived in Rome.~~ → She told me she **had lived** in Rome.
structure:
## Формы
| | Утверждение | Отрицание | Вопрос |
|---|---|---|---|
| Past perfect | She had left. | She hadn't left. | Had she left? |
| Краткая форма | She'd left. | She'd not left. | — |

## Формулы
> past simple (точка отсчёта) + **past perfect** (раньше)
> When he called, I had already gone.

> **Hardly / Scarcely** + had + subject + V3 + **when** ...
> Hardly had it started when it stopped.

> **No sooner** + had + subject + V3 + **than** ...
> No sooner had we sat down than the lights went out.

> **By the time** + past simple, past perfect
> By the time we got there, they had gone.

## Сравнительная таблица
| Значение | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Раньше опорной точки | past perfect | I had eaten when she arrived. |
| Последовательность (ясна) | past simple | I ate and then she arrived. |
| Причина состояния | past perfect | He was tired; he had worked all night. |
| Нереализованное намерение | had hoped / intended | I had hoped to win. |
| Первый раз | first time + past perfect | It was the first time I had skied. |
| Косвенная речь | past perfect | She said she had won. |

exercises.title: Past perfect или past simple?
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол в past perfect или past simple.
exercises.example: When we got there, the film (start). → had started.

items.text: When we {{got}} to the cinema, the film {{had already started|'d already started}}.
She {{was}} exhausted because she {{hadn't slept|had not slept}} for two days.
After he {{had finished|'d finished|finished}} his degree, he {{moved}} to Singapore.
I {{had never seen|'d never seen}} snow before I moved to Canada.
By the time the ambulance {{arrived}}, the patient {{had died|'d died}}.
He {{told}} me he {{had lost|'d lost}} his wallet on the train.
I {{realised|realized}} I {{had left|'d left}} my keys in the office.
By 2010, the company {{had opened|'d opened}} offices in twelve countries.

exercises.title: Планы, инверсия, причины
exercises.instruction: Вставьте пропущенное слово или поставьте глагол в past perfect (или past simple, где указано).

items.text: Hardly {{had}} the meeting begun when the fire alarm went off.
No sooner had we left {{than}} it started to pour.
She {{had hoped|'d hoped}} to finish the marathon, but she twisted her ankle at mile ten.
It was the first time I {{had flown|'d flown}} alone.
He didn't answer because he {{hadn't heard|had not heard}} the phone.
Once the guests {{had left|'d left|left}}, we cleaned up.
I {{had been|'d been}} to Rome before, so I knew my way around.
She was upset. Her boss {{had criticised|had criticized|'d criticised|'d criticized}} her in front of everyone.

exercises.title: Выберите правильную форму
exercises.instruction: Выберите вариант, который лучше всего подходит по смыслу.

items.q: When I called, Ines ___ already left.
She was nervous because she ___ the exam twice before.
I ___ to the door, and then I realised I had no key.
items.why: Два действия по порядку — **past simple**; past perfect нужен только для события, которое было раньше опорной точки.

items.q: Before I ___ the office, I locked the door.
items.why: Порядок задан словом **before**, поэтому достаточно past simple.

items.q: I was surprised to see Tom. I thought he ___ to Berlin.
She ___ the door and walked in.
By the time I got to the party, everyone ___.
items.why: **By the time** + past simple → в главной части past perfect.

items.q: Hardly ___ the speech started when the microphone failed.

options: When I arrived, the train already left.
When I arrived, the train had already left.
items.why: Поезд ушёл до моего приезда — past perfect.

options: I recognised her because I saw her photo before.
I recognised her because I had seen her photo before.
She told me that she has lived in Rome before.
She told me that she had lived in Rome before.
items.why: В косвенной речи после told — сдвиг времён: **had lived**.

options: As soon as he had left, she turned on the radio.
As soon as he had left, she has turned on the radio.
items.why: Рассказ в прошлом: past perfect + past simple.

options: No sooner I had sat down than the phone rang.
No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.
After they had eaten, they went for a walk.
After they had eaten, they had gone for a walk.
items.why: Прогулка — события в порядке рассказа, она в past simple; had нужен только для более раннего действия.

exercises.title: Составьте предложения
exercises.instruction: Составьте предложение из слов, используя past perfect и past simple.

items.prompt: (when / I / get to the station / the train / already / leave)
answers: When I got to the station, the train had already left.
When I got to the station the train had already left.
The train had already left when I got to the station.

items.prompt: (she / be / upset / because / she / lose / her job)
answers: She was upset because she had lost her job.
She was upset because she'd lost her job.

items.prompt: (we / be / lost / because / we / forget / the map)
answers: We were lost because we had forgotten the map.
We were lost because we'd forgotten the map.

items.prompt: (he / admit / that / he / never / read / the contract)
answers: He admitted that he had never read the contract.
He admitted that he'd never read the contract.
He admitted he had never read the contract.
He admitted he'd never read the contract.

items.prompt: (hardly / the film / begin / when / the power / go out)
answers: Hardly had the film begun when the power went out.

items.prompt: (by the time / we / arrive / the shop / close)
answers: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.
By the time we arrived the shop had closed.

items.prompt: I finished my homework. Then I watched TV. → I watched TV after I ...
answers: I watched TV after I had finished my homework.
I watched TV after I'd finished my homework.

items.prompt: They sold all the tickets, so we couldn't get any. → We couldn't get tickets because they ...
answers: We couldn't get tickets because they had sold out.
We couldn't get tickets because they'd sold out.
We couldn't get tickets because they had sold all the tickets.
We couldn't get tickets because they'd sold all the tickets.

items.prompt: I planned to call you, but I forgot. (mean) → I ... to call you, but I forgot.
answers: I had meant to call you, but I forgot.
I'd meant to call you, but I forgot.

items.prompt: It was my first time in Japan. → I (never / be) ... to Japan before.
answers: I had never been to Japan before.
I'd never been to Japan before.

items.prompt: 'I've lost my passport,' she said. → She said (that) she ...
answers: She said she had lost her passport.
She said she'd lost her passport.
She said that she had lost her passport.
She said that she'd lost her passport.

items.prompt: 'We've already eaten,' they told us. → They told us that they ...
answers: They told us that they had already eaten.
They told us that they'd already eaten.
They told us they had already eaten.
They told us they'd already eaten.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте на вопросы полными предложениями на английском, используя past perfect там, где нужно.

items.prompt: Think of a time you arrived somewhere and something had already happened. What was it?
items.sample: When I got to the airport, my flight had already been delayed for two hours.

items.prompt: Describe something you had hoped to do but couldn't.
items.sample: I had hoped to visit Japan last spring, but I couldn't get time off work.

items.prompt: Explain why you felt a certain way yesterday (use because + past perfect).
items.sample: I felt exhausted yesterday because I hadn't slept well the night before.

items.prompt: Describe your first time doing something important (It was the first time I had...).
items.sample: It was the first time I had spoken to a large audience, and my hands were shaking.

items.prompt: Write about something that had changed when you returned to a place after a long time.
items.sample: When I returned to my hometown, they had built a new shopping centre where the park used to be.
